haiku-low.q1: Only the most recent fire time is kept; the older ones are dropped with no history entries. One run is created for it.
haiku-low.q2: The new run is inserted with status skipped. It is never executed and has no attempts.
haiku-low.q3: At most 3 attempts. Wait 1 minute before attempt 2 and 5 minutes before attempt 3. After the third failure, the run becomes failed.
haiku-low.q4: After the lease expires, 2 minutes after the last heartbeat, the reaper marks the attempt lost and the run retries after the wait. Yes, it uses an attempt.
haiku-low.q5: The running job finishes normally. Its pending runs are marked cancelled. Fire times during the pause get no runs or history. On resume, next_fire_at is set to the first fire time after now.
haiku-low.q6: The unique constraint on (schedule_id, scheduled_for) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING stops duplicate runs. FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED also lets only one worker handle a schedule at a time.
haiku-low.q7: In JOB_SCHEDULE.next_fire_at. It changes when run creation handles a due schedule, and when a schedule is re-enabled or a tenant resumed, set to the first fire time after now.
haiku-low.q8: One atomic statement picks the oldest due pending run with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. It sets running, lease owner, lease expiry, increments attempt_count, and inserts a running attempt.
haiku-low.q9: Kept in JOB_RUN as lease_owner and lease_expires_at. The reaper notices staleness by finding running runs whose lease_expires_at is in the past.
haiku-low.q10: Recorded in the run's available_at. The retry starts when a worker claims the pending run once available_at is at or before now.
haiku-low.q11: Once per fire time: the JOB_RUN row, unique on (schedule_id, scheduled_for). Once per execution try: the RUN_ATTEMPT row.
haiku-low.q12: Its fence check fails because lease_owner and attempt_count no longer match, since each claim increments attempt_count. So its write changes nothing.

sonnet.q1: Only the most recent missed fire time becomes a run (pending, available at its fire time); the two older ones are dropped with no history entries. Then next_fire_at moves to the first fire time after now.
sonnet.q2: It is inserted as a run with status 'skipped'. It is never executed and has no attempts. The skipped run stays in history.
sonnet.q3: Up to 3 attempts. Wait is 1 minute before attempt 2 and 5 minutes before attempt 3. After the third failed attempt the run becomes 'failed'.
sonnet.q4: The lease expires 2 minutes after the last heartbeat. The reaper then marks the attempt 'lost', clears lease_owner and sets the run back to pending after the wait, so another worker can claim it once available_at passes. Yes, the lost attempt counts toward the 3-attempt limit (if attempt_count is already 3, the run becomes failed).
sonnet.q5: The running job is not touched and finishes normally. The pending run is marked 'cancelled' and stays in history. When the tenant is resumed, next_fire_at is set to the first fire time after now. Fire times that passed during the pause are not run and get no history entries.
sonnet.q6: The FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED lock on the schedule means only one worker handles it at a time. As a backstop, the unique constraint on JOB_RUN (schedule_id, scheduled_for) plus ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING means a second insert does nothing, so no duplicate run is made.
sonnet.q7: In the next_fire_at column of the JOB_SCHEDULE row. It is set after runs are created, to the first fire time after the current time, computed in the schedule's timezone. It is also reset to the first fire time after now when a schedule is re-enabled or a tenant is resumed.
sonnet.q8: One single database statement picks the oldest pending run with available_at <= now() using FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so other workers skip it. In the same statement it sets status running, sets lease_owner and lease_expires_at, increments attempt_count and inserts a RUN_ATTEMPT row. The worker starts the job only after the claim succeeds.
sonnet.q9: In the JOB_RUN row, in lease_owner and lease_expires_at, which each heartbeat (every 30 seconds) pushes forward. The reaper, a periodic check that any worker can run, notices running runs whose lease_expires_at is in the past.
sonnet.q10: The wait is recorded in the JOB_RUN row's available_at (now plus 1 minute before attempt 2, or 5 minutes before attempt 3), with status back to pending. The retry starts when a worker's normal claim statement picks it up once available_at <= now().
sonnet.q11: Once per fire time: a JOB_RUN row (unique on schedule_id plus scheduled_for). Once per execution try: a RUN_ATTEMPT row (unique on run_id plus attempt_no).
sonnet.q12: The fence check. Its write only applies if the worker ID (lease_owner) and attempt count still match the values it got at claim time. They no longer match after takeover (claims increment attempt_count), so its write changes nothing.
